episodes.214501: A backdoor front pushed through northeast and east-central NM and ended up along the east slopes of the central mountain chain come midday July 31st. Higher moisture behind the front, and lift along the front resulted in thunderstorm development across the central mountain chain during the early afternoon. Storms congealed into a line as they moved east and southeast across the eastern highlands and plains resulting in severe thunderstorm wind gusts near Cuero in Guadalupe County, Tucumcari and Clayton Municipal Airports, and a mesonet station in far northeast Lincoln County. The line also resulted in thunderstorm wind damage at a CoCoRaHS observer's residence south of Fort Sumner. The line of thunderstorms moved southeast into west Texas during the mid to late evening hours while the backdoor front pushed through the gaps of the central mountain chain resulting in gusty east canyon winds across the Santa Fe and Albuquerque Metros.
episodes.214718: A decaying cluster of storms moved into northern portions of the area during the late evening/overnight hours of the 31st. These storms had produced a strong outflow boundary, which moved across the area and produced severe wind gusts in several locations. Strong to severe gusts persisted for over an hour in some locations after the boundary moved through and storms had decayed.
episodes.214719: A decaying cluster of storms moved into northern portions of the area during the late evening/overnight hours of the 31st. These storms had produced a strong outflow boundary, which moved across the area and produced severe wind gusts in several locations. Strong to severe gusts persisted for over an hour in some locations after the boundary moved through and storms had decayed.
episodes.214747: By the middle of the afternoon of the 31st, a cold front stalled out across the extreme southern Texas Panhandle. Strong surface heating ahead of the front allowed storms to develop along the leading edge of the front creating severe wind gusts in Childress County. A second round of storms came during the evening hours from the west. Thunderstorms initially developed off of the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico into the Raton Mesa. As these storms progressed southeastward they eventually grew upscale along numerous outflow boundaries spreading into the South Plains. A dry sub-cloud layer allowed these storms to become outflow dominant creating numerous severe wind gusts through the late evening hours.
episodes.214946: Scattered slow moving thunderstorms produced some minor road flooding in Dale county.
episodes.216199: A few isolated severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts on the evening of July 31 across portions of south central Missouri. There were a few reports of trees downed or damaged across Texas and Shannon counties.
episodes.216286: A storm system moved across the area during the late afternoon and evening hours on the 31st and brought scattered storms to the area during the afternoon and evening. These storms produced several clouds.  One of these storms produced a tornado near the Cedar Rapids Eastern Iowa Airport. This tornado was rated EFU because there was no visible damage.
episodes.217044: An upper high was located over southern New Mexico with some modest mid-level moisture present.  The location of the upper high kept thunderstorm motion very slow and over an inch and a half of rain was reported in the area.
episodes.217045: An upper high over southern New Mexico but with modest mid level moisture and high temperatures over 105 degrees helped produce gusty thunderstorms over El Paso with wind gusts up to 64 mph.
episodes.217207: During the afternoon a broken line of severe thunderstorms moved southeast through central and southeast Missouri. On its track, a few cells produced 3 tornadoes as well as tree and structural damage.

events.narrative: A utility company reported a loss of 11 steel transmission structures due to a microburst producing thunderstorm near Kirkland. It was reported that the structures were rated for 100 mph winds.
There was standing water on the roadway at 523 Mary McClendon Rd.

A CoCoRaHS observer south of Fort Sumner reported significant wind gusts that blew tree limbs down in her property.  The severe thunderstorm winds knocked out electricity for several hours after the storm blew through.
Emergency Manager reported several large tree branches downed due to wind.

The Emergency Manager reported a long lived funnel cloud associated with a  storm southwest of Cedar Rapids resulted in  a brief touchdown just north of the Eastern  Iowa Airport. This was an EFU tornado, as  there is no known damage, with photos and  videos indicating a very brief touch down.
The Biggs Field AWOS recorded a peak gust of 63 mph.
The El Paso Airport recorded a peak gust of 64 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Friona measured severe wind gusts from 1903 CST through 1926 CST. A peak gust of 75 mph was measured at 1905 CST.
A trained spotter reported a funnel cloud that was close to the  ground northeast of Springville.
A report of trees downed at the Pulltite Campground along the Current River.
Flooding was reported along Stern Drive and Las Alturas Drive as well as the Interstate 10 frontage roads between Peter Hurd Road and Mesquite.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Dimmitt measured intermittent severe wind gusts from 1950 CST through 2013 CST. A peak wind gust of 63 mph was measured at 1950 CST.
The Roswell No. 2 Portable mesonet station measured a 59 mph wind gust from a nearby thunderstorm. Time is estimated based on radar.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Morton measured severe wind gusts from 2027 CST through 2106 CST. A peak wind gust of 67 mph was measured 2030 CST.
An EF1 tornado formed along Stoney Point Rd and briefly tracked southeastward, producing sporadic tree damage and minor structural damage before dissipating over Lac Capri.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Tulia measured a severe wind gust of 62 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Abernathy measured severe wind gusts from 2036 CST through 2037 CST with a peak gust of 68 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Hart measured severe wind gusts from 2036 CST through 2043 CST. A peak wind gust of 77 mph was measured at 2039 CST.

Thunderstorm winds caused a swath of wind damage in St. Francois County. Damage extended as far north as 2 SSE Valles Mill and as far south as 2S Doe Run. Most of the damage done was to trees, with several reports of downed trees blocking roads around the County. Near Doe Run, winds damaged the roof siding of a home and lifted and destroyed a gazebo. In Farmington, winds caused minor damage to the siding and gutter of a home.
Mesonet station 51 2SW Tatum NM measured a 66 mph wind gust, along with several other gusts over 58 mph.

Emergency management reported damage to a canopy and temporary fencing at a fair in  Lovington. Some downed power lines were also reported in the area. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar. The cost of damage and the maximum wind gust are also estimated.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Wolfforth measured a severe wind gust of 58 mph.
Mesonet station 66 Hobbs, NM/ Lea County measured a 58 mph wind gust.
Mesonet station 15 Seagraves 1SW measured a 62 mph wind gust behind a strong  thunderstorm outflow boundary.
Timing is approximated from radar. Report on social media from storm spotters of tree damage from an estimated 60 mph wind gust. The cost of damage is also approximated.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near White River Lake measured severe wind gusts from 2237 CST through 2238 CST with a peak gust of 62 mph.
Mesonet station 18 Lamesa 2SE measured a 68 mph wind gust associated with strong  thunderstorm outflow.
